named_events.event_name: Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria and Mexican Earthquake (HIMM)
named_events.loss_description: The net impact of HIMM is GBP 12.5m. The accounts most impacted by HIMM are cargo, marine and non-marine property.
had only limited exposure to the California wildfires and no losses from the subsequent mudslides.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate shows a small favourable prior-year development on older underwriting years (primarily the 2015 underwriting year) of approximately GBP 0.56m (a c.1.27% release relative to opening gross claims outstanding). This prior-year improvement is calculated from the gross claims development table. Broader reserve movements in 2016-2017 were driven by catastrophe events (notably HIMM) and large individual losses, but the quantified prior-year movement in the gross triangle is a modest release.
raw_causal_phrases: a combination of a large loss of GBP 1.6m and a higher than expected incidence of attritional claims.
two catastrophe losses which impacted the portfolio disproportionately.
The net impact of HIMM is GBP 12.5m.
Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria (HIM) all feature in the top ten most expensive losses suffered by Lloyd's.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure (-0.557m) is calculated from the gross claims development triangle (gross presentation in GBP 7000s) for the 2015 underwriting year (comparison of the 12-month and 24-month diagonals). No explicit textual statement of a gross prior-year movement was found; calculation is therefore used (confidence 0.8). The triangle is presented as outflows (values in parentheses). Movements for 2016 and 2017 were excluded per methodology. No per-line-of-business gross prior-year movements quantified in the report.
